takeaway: Classic rainy-season week: hot, sticky mornings, then afternoon storms, and Costa Rica's weather service says rain may hang on into the evening in Guanacaste today. A tropical wave arrives Friday and boosts the odds of morning rain on the coast Thursday through Sunday. For surf, winds stay light and variable today and Wednesday, then turn northwest (side-onshore at Nosara) Thursday into the weekend, so dawn is the only clean window. A long-period southwest swell builds from Wednesday. The models hint at real Caribbean trade winds (offshore for us) coming back around Oct 11–13. No storms threaten Costa Rica; the main system is forming off southern Mexico. Multi-day soaking rain is still watch-only, with one model family wetter for Oct 12–17.

periods.label: Days 1–3 (Tue–Thu)
periods.pattern: Normal rainy-season rhythm. Today starts partly cloudy and muggy, with showers and storms in the afternoon and scattered rain lingering into the first part of the night. Nicoya tops out around 34°C. Wednesday and Thursday look similar, with light to moderate daily rain in the averages and heavier storms favoring the mountains. Monday's storms dropped 40–80 mm on the Guanacaste mountains, per the weather service.
periods.implications: Mornings are the window for anything outdoors. Plan around afternoon thunderstorms and expect some evenings to stay wet today. Surf: light winds early, chop building after midday.
periods.confidence: High on the morning-dry, afternoon-storm pattern. Moderate on exactly when cells hit Nosara.

periods.label: Days 4–7 (Fri–Mon, Oct 9–12)
periods.pattern: A tropical wave passes Friday. With unsettled air over the nearby Pacific, the weather service gives better odds of morning rain along the coast Thursday through Sunday, plus scattered afternoon storms, some heavy. Model averages turn a bit wetter over the weekend, especially just offshore and on the Caribbean side. By Sunday and Monday, every model family strengthens the east-to-northeast trade winds across Nicaragua and northern Costa Rica.
periods.implications: Keep weekend plans flexible. Rain can come early in the day, not just afternoons. If the trades build as shown, surf mornings should clean up noticeably from about Sunday or Monday.
periods.confidence: Moderate on the wave bringing a wetter Friday to Sunday. Moderate on the trade-wind return, low on its exact day.

periods.label: Days 8–15 (Oct 13–20)
periods.pattern: The models split. The European AI ensemble keeps steady trade winds and drier weather on our Pacific side, with rain favoring the Caribbean coast. The U.S. ensemble is clearly wetter, with broad low pressure over southern Central America around Oct 13–17 and heavier daily rain across Costa Rica. The standard European ensemble sits in between: wet offshore around Oct 12–14, then moderate. The U.S. hurricane center sees a low forming south of Guatemala early next week (20% chance of development) that drifts away west-northwest. Costa Rica's long-range outlook calls for less rain than normal Oct 12–18, no extreme events, and very dry weather after about Oct 26.
periods.implications: Next week could go either way: drier with offshore trades, or a stretch of wetter days if the U.S. model's broad low comes true. Don't lock in rain-sensitive plans for Oct 13–17 yet.
periods.confidence: Low to moderate. The official outlook leans drier, but model spread is high.

surfWinds.regime: Light/variable, then Pacific northwest (side-onshore) through Saturday. Caribbean trades (offshore) may return around Oct 11–13.
surfWinds.detail: Papagayo marine forecast (issued 1:44 a.m. PDT Tuesday): variable winds under 5 knots today and Wednesday, going northwest around 10 knots late at night. Then northwest to north about 10 knots Thursday through Saturday. At Nosara, northwest is side-onshore, so expect texture and chop once it fills in. Light and variable does not mean glassy offshore. It just means no trade wind; the sea breeze still takes over by late morning. Seas 3–5 ft from the west-northwest today, then a southwest swell with 16–17 second periods builds 4–6 ft Wednesday into the weekend. Nicaragua: the trades are blowing over Nicaragua's interior and Caribbean side, but they aren't reaching the Pacific coast at the surface this week, so there's no all-day offshore quality signal yet. The models agree the trades strengthen and push out over the Gulf of Papagayo around Oct 11–13, strongest in the European AI ensemble. That would mean clean Nosara mornings, not necessarily all-day offshore.
surfWinds.bestWindows: Dawn patrol every day this week, before the sea breeze and the Thursday-on northwest wind. The new southwest swell (Wed–Sat) is the main event, so go early. Watch Sunday Oct 11 to Tuesday Oct 13 for a better trade-wind morning glass setup.
surfWinds.confidence: High on light winds turning northwest through Saturday. Moderate on the swell timing. Low to moderate on when the trades return.

gyreWatch.status: Watch only, a notch higher for Oct 12–17. Nothing established.
gyreWatch.possibleTiming: Oct 12–17 is the window to watch, mainly from the U.S. ensemble. Nothing is set up near Costa Rica this week.
gyreWatch.supporting: The U.S. ensemble shows broad low pressure and heavier rain over Costa Rica and the nearby Pacific Oct 13–17. The standard European ensemble is wet just offshore Oct 12–14 and shows a low south of Guatemala around Oct 18. The U.S. hurricane center expects a low to form south of Guatemala early next week. The U.S. tropics outlook (from 29 Sep, valid Oct 7–20) mentioned possible Central American gyre formation early in its window.
gyreWatch.conflicting: The European AI ensemble keeps firm trade winds instead, which usually means a drier Pacific side and wetter Caribbean coast. Costa Rica's weather service forecasts less rain than normal Oct 12–18 with no extreme events, turning very dry after Oct 26. The system off Mexico pulls away from us. That U.S. tropics outlook is a week old (new one due today).

whatChanged: Changes since Sunday's briefing (Monday's didn't publish): The weather service now expects tropical wave #50 on Friday, with morning coastal rain chances Thursday through Sunday. Sunday's outlook said no waves were coming. Monday's storms were heavier than expected, 40–80 mm in the Guanacaste mountains. Surf winds: the brief Wednesday easterly from Sunday's forecast is gone. It's now light/variable, then northwest from Thursday, plus a new long-period southwest swell. The models now show trades returning around Oct 11–13. The Mexico system is now 90% likely to develop within 48 hours (up from 50%). The hurricane center added a new low south of Guatemala early next week (20%). The weather service's long-range outlook now runs Oct 12–Nov 8 and is drier, very dry after Oct 26. Rain watch: still watch-only, but the U.S. ensemble is wetter for Oct 12–17.
practical: Do outdoor stuff in the morning. Expect afternoon storms, with some evening rain today, and keep Thursday through Sunday mornings flexible around the Friday tropical wave. Surf at dawn: the southwest swell builds Wednesday, and northwest wind adds texture from Thursday. The best bet for clean offshore mornings is around Oct 11–13 if the trades show up. No tropical storm threat to Costa Rica. Re-check later this week on the Oct 13–17 wet-versus-trades split.
